subject: Infra & Unit Econ: QBR prep sync — launch plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@cloudvendor.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR: infra / unit economics sync (draft ask)

Team —

As we lock the QBR narrative, leadership wants a tight infra + unit-econ section that shows: current GPU spend and normalized unit cost, utilization profile by pool, and the expected delta from recommended batching + KV caching changes. High-level asks:

- GPU spend last 6 months (by pool + committed vs. burst).
- GPU utilization distribution (p50/p90/p99; GPU minutes consumed by low-latency vs batch jobs).
- Current cache hit rates and prefix reuse metrics (by customer cohort).
- Quantized model performance (latency & cost delta) where we've already tested it.

I'm proposing a single slide that ties these to the OKR: reduce token cost per 1k inference by 15% while preserving p99 latency SLAs. Can Marcus own the raw numbers and a first-pass spreadsheet? Grace / Laura, can you coordinate the narrative and what product/ops asks we want to surface (rollout timing, SLA exceptions, dedicated commits ask)?

I'll pull in Marketplace Ops for cloud cost reconciliation on committed vs burst billing — cc'd.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> As we lock the QBR narrative, leadership wants a tight infra + unit-econ section that shows: current GPU spend and normalized unit cost, utilization profile by pool, and the expected delta from recommended batching + KV caching changes.

Thanks — I'm on it. I started a working workbook (attached) with: spend by sku/pool, effective $/GPU-hour after committed discounts, and token-level cost based on our muxed model-of-requests.

Quick notes / asks for data completeness:
- Grace: need mapping of customers to low-latency vs batch routing (CSV) so I can split utilization.
- Laura: can you pull the OKR target language so I can align the cost-per-token baseline?
- Vivek: any preferred normalization for model families (e.g., per-1k tokens at 2048 seq)?

I'll also include an experiment tab showing estimated unit-cost impact from: 1) 2x batching (latency tradeoff table), 2) KV prefix caching at 30/50/70% hit rates, 3) switch to 8-bit quantized kernels for eligible models. The workbook includes formulae and assumptions.

Attaching: gpu-spend-breakdown-v2.xlsx

—Marcus
Sr. Director, Compute Economics

Subject: Re: QBR: infra / unit economics sync (draft ask)

Thanks all — pulling this together as the "launchpad" doc for the infra slide. Action items and owners below, please confirm: 

1) Marcus — finalize numbers sheet (gpu-spend-breakdown-v2.xlsx) + include a short assumptions tab. Deliverable: workbook + two charts (spend trend, normalized $/1k tokens). Due: Fri 12/04 EOD.
2) Marcus & Diane — run an experiments sheet for batching vs cache hit-rate scenarios (include latency penalty estimates at p50/p90/p99). Deliverable: experiment tab. Due: Mon 12/07 AM.
3) Laura — craft the OKR tie-in + a 75-word executive blurb that calls out the ask (commitments, recommended cadence). Deliverable: blurb for the slide. Due: Tue 12/08.
4) Grace — assemble slide deck draft, pull in CM and CS asks (I will collate marketplace reconciliation items). Deliverable: qbr-slide-deck-draft.pptx. Due: Wed 12/09 for leadership review.

Diane (copied) — can you validate the latency estimation approach for batching impact and confirm if our assumptions on p99 degradation per batch size are plausible?

Also flagged: we will ask for a short one-time dedicated commit to cover predictable traffic for tier-1 customers — need numbers to justify.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR: infra / unit economics sync (draft ask)

Adding a few specifics to ensure the slide answers leadership questions: 

- Please include p99 latency impact lines for the recommended batching settings and for a conservative KV cache hit (use 30% and 50% as anchors).
- Show committed vs. on-demand effective $/GPU-hour and the net savings if we move 40% of traffic to reserved pools.
- Include a single-case study: Scalesys's projected cost with our recommendations (they gave permission to anonymize). Marcus — can you slot that into the workbook?

One more ask: can we call out any operational risk (fallback behavior) if cache hit drops below 20% after rollout? Leadership wants to see mitigations.

I'll draft the 75-word blurb and drop it into the shared Drive by EOD Monday.

—Laura
Group Product Lead, Performance & Cost

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR: infra / unit economics sync (draft ask)

All — quick status: workbook updated with Scalesys anonymized scenario, three experiment tabs (batch x2, cache at 30/50/70%, quantization delta). Slides holder created in drive and draft deck attached (qbr-slide-deck-draft.pptx).

Diane validated the latency assumptions (see her inline comments on the experiments tab). For the p99 penalty I modeled conservative degradation of 8-15ms at 2x batching for interactive models and larger for long-seq batch jobs — documented in the notes.

Next steps: practice run scheduled Tues 12/07 10:00–10:45 (invite in calendar). Grace — I'll be ready with the charts.

—Marcus
Sr. Director, Compute Economics
